trust_decision.summary: The upload allow-list accepts .svg as both an asset and a profile image. The bytes then go through sharp/libvips, whose bundled ImageMagick coders (from the external base image) decide what the file may load. The in-repo fix commit changes no source; it only bumps versions (fix.diff:1-178).

landing_point.why: The summary says 'SVG upload'. The SVG entry in the image allow-list is the first in-repo place an engineer would look.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The fix sits outside this repository, in the immich-app/base-images build referenced by digest at server/Dockerfile:1 and server/Dockerfile:89. Not inspectable in scope.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue that SVG is a documented supported format (mime-types.ts:62) and that the coder policy belongs to the container image, not the app code.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: SVG stays a supported asset and profile format, and sharp keeps decoding the other image formats. Dropping SVG or disabling magickload wholesale would break legitimate uploads (e.g. RAW/HEIC handled by other loaders).

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Profile-image upload: an .svg passes isProfile and goes to sharp via generateProfileImage
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Profile images look like a neighbouring feature, separate from asset upload
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different service file from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: OAuth profile picture: a fetched image goes through generateProfileImage
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Content is supplied by the identity provider, not by an upload
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: auth service, separate from the upload path

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Image metadata probe: sharp().metadata() runs on the original before the thumbnail pipeline
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It only reads metadata and does not decode
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same repository file as the decode pipeline

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A loader or format allow-list on the sharp() constructor, enforced on only one of the two sharp() call sites
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Two separate sharp() constructions exist (lines 187 and 415). A maintainer hardening the decode pipeline could easily miss the metadata probe.

O9_family: code injection via an image-decoder delegate (ImageMagick coders reached from SVG through libvips); the fix lives in the external runtime image

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + pnpm, NestJS server; sharp/libvips/ImageMagick come from the ghcr.io/immich-app/base-server-* images
O10_build.project_tests: server/src/utils/mime-types.spec.ts, server/src/services/asset-media.service.spec.ts, server/src/services/media.service.spec.ts (unit, mocked media repository; the ImageMagick behaviour is not exercised)

j.j_sites_touched: none (version-bump files only: package.json files, pubspec.yaml, Info.plist, Fastfile, openapi spec, fetch-client.ts header)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Remove '.svg' from the allow-list in mime-types.ts. That breaks the supported SVG format and leaves the external coder policy untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The actual remediation is most likely in immich-app/base-images (ImageMagick policy or the libvips build). The pinned commit itself is the base-image update to 202609281550 (server/Dockerfile:1,89), so the pinned tree may already carry the fixed runtime. Not checkable without another repository.
unverified: The fix diff (fix.diff:1-178) contains only version bumps. No source change addresses the advisory, so there are no fix sites to compare. The host is unusable as a published-fix task.
Whether the pinned base-image digest is the vulnerable or the fixed image: unknown (external repository).
The O8 routes reach the same sharp sink, but the protection is not an in-repo check, so 'protection applied' cannot be judged from this tree.
No red flag's literal definition holds: single_site requires one changed function, but the fix changes zero. The disqualifier is that the fix is absent from the source.
Repo size and offline buildability were not measured.
